structure Meshes (P : ℕ → Table C.book) : Prop where
  continuous {n : ℕ} (p : ℕ) (v : Fin n → C.book.Token) :
    ContinuousOn (fun x => (P p).read x v) (Cyclic C.S p n)
  onK (p n : ℕ) (K : Set (Points n)) (h : IsCompact K) (hk : K ⊆ Cyclic C.S p n) (v : Fin n → C.book.Token) :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ i : ℕ in atTop, ∀ r : Fin n → Cover, grid C (f.mesh i) r ∈ K →
      ‖(C.numeric (f.mesh i) p v (fun j => wrap _ (r j))) - (P p).read (grid C (f.mesh i) r) v‖ < ε

verdicts.summary: [L] proves less than [M] prints. [M] prints `\partial_{\boldsymbol l}f_{P(k),v}\longrightarrow \partial_{\boldsymbol l}S_n(v;\cdot) \quad\text{locally uniformly on }\Conf{n}`.
evidence: [M] prints S_n(v;.) in C^infty(Conf_n) and convergence of every derivative d_l f_{P(k),v} to d_l S_n locally uniformly on Conf_n. [L] gives smoothness on conf n of a table T (Table.Smooth: ContDiffOn R inf ... (conf n)) via Arrives.serves/Cleaner, and RawLimits.volume = VolumePoints only states value convergence ||(P (f.per i)).read x v - S.read x v|| < eps on compact K with K subset generic n (all coordinate projections injective, strictly smaller than conf n), with the P p only ContinuousOn Cyclic. No declaration in Extraction/, Dash/ or Org/ states convergence of derivatives of the finite-volume tables or their smoothness, so the smoothness half matches but the convergence half is weaker (derivative order 0 only, and on generic rather than Conf_n); not a typo.

M prints S_n in C^infty(Conf_n) and convergence of every derivative d_l f_{P(k),v} to d_l S_n, locally uniformly on Conf_n. L's RawLimits has only `regular : ContinuousOn ... (generic n)` and `volume : VolumePoints`, which is value-level (`‖(P (f.per i)).read x v - S.read x v‖ < ε` on compact K ⊆ generic n); smoothness is obtained only for a replacement table T via Dash.awake (matchReg + T.Smooth) and Arrives.serves, agreeing with S only on generic points, and no declaration states derivative convergence of the P tables. M's proof (Arzela-Ascoli with equicontinuity from derivative bounds, diagonalizing over derivative lists) is not written in L, so this is not a typo but a real gap.
